definitions.explanation: In baseball, a complete game in which the pitcher allows no batter to reach base at all — no hits, no walks, no errors — retiring every opposing hitter in order.

examples.japanese: {完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}を{達成|たっせい}する。
{完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}は{めった}に{出|で}ない{記録|きろく}だ。
examples.english: A perfect game is a record that rarely happens.

examples.japanese: {九回|きゅうかい}{二死|にし}まで{完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}だったが、{最後|さいご}に{一本|いっぽん}{打|う}たれた。
examples.english: It was a perfect game until two outs in the ninth, but he gave up a hit at the very end.

notes:
A baseball term for the rarest kind of dominant pitching: not a single opposing batter reaches base. Stricter than a no-hitter, which still allows walks and errors.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}を{達成|たっせい}する: to achieve a perfect game
- {完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}{達成|たっせい}{投手|とうしゅ}: the pitcher who threw the perfect game

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ノーヒットノーラン: no-hitter — no hits allowed, but walks or errors may let runners on base
- {完封|かんぷう}: shutout — allowing no runs, though base runners are permitted
